user_story.capability: the fetcher to obtain Amtrak's Service Alerts & Notices page using a real browser
user_story.benefit: Akamai-protected advisory content becomes available to the feed

criteria.trigger: the fetcher begins a poll cycle
criteria.behavior: load the Amtrak Service Alerts & Notices page in a real browser that executes the page's JavaScript
produce output containing the `na-service-alert__*` advisory markup that the service's parsers consume

criteria.trigger: the browser does not obtain the advisory markup within a bounded per-cycle timeout
criteria.behavior: abort the cycle without overwriting a previously valid snapshot

user_story.capability: the fetcher to write the advisories to the location and format the service already consumes

criteria.trigger: a poll cycle obtains the advisory markup
criteria.behavior: write it to the snapshot source the service reads via `AdvisoryConfig.url`
make the write atomic so a reader observes either the complete previous snapshot or the complete new one
update the snapshot's freshness marker so the service can detect staleness through its existing TTL

criteria.trigger: the feed-producer service reads a fetcher-produced snapshot
criteria.behavior: emit the scoped station and route alerts the existing parsers derive from that markup

user_story.capability: a fetcher failure to never break the feed
user_story.benefit: advisories are a best-effort enhancement rather than a dependency

criteria.trigger: the fetcher cannot produce a fresh snapshot
criteria.behavior: continue serving feeds using the last snapshot or none, without a failed generation

criteria.trigger: the fetcher process crashes or is killed
criteria.behavior: continue serving feeds unaffected

user_story.capability: the fetcher to use little memory and recover from crashes on its own
user_story.benefit: it runs unattended on a shared device without needing a hard cap

criteria.behavior: launch a single browser instance at a time so its peak memory stays bounded to one browser rather than growing across cycles
close the browser so that no browser process remains resident between polls

criteria.trigger: the fetcher process crashes or is terminated
criteria.behavior: restart and resume polling without manual intervention

user_story.capability: the browser confined to the fetcher image
user_story.benefit: the feed-producer service keeps its scratch/musl, no-vulnerabilities container posture

criteria.behavior: remain free of any browser or browser runtime dependency
package the browser and its dependencies only within its own container image

user_story.benefit: it neither hammers Amtrak nor draws bot-defense attention

criteria.behavior: wait at least that interval between successive page loads
default its poll interval to the order of the service's static-data refresh rather than a sub-minute rate

user_story.capability: the spike to decide the approach before the component is built
user_story.benefit: we do not invest in a sidecar that cannot work or cannot fit the device

criteria.behavior: report whether a server-IP browser obtains the `na-service-alert__*` markup and the success rate over repeated cycles on ARM64
demonstrate at least three consecutive successful retrievals to establish repeatability rather than a single success

criteria.trigger: the spike cannot obtain the markup repeatably from a server IP
criteria.behavior: fall back to the managed-API approach or shelve the feature, without building the sidecar or changing the service image

user_story.benefit: it costs almost nothing to run continuously on the Pi alongside other workloads

criteria.behavior: run no browser process and perform no work beyond waiting for the next scheduled poll

criteria.trigger: a freshly fetched advisory document is identical to the current snapshot's content
criteria.behavior: refresh the snapshot's freshness marker without rewriting the snapshot payload

criteria.trigger: a poll cycle completes or aborts
criteria.behavior: release all browser and temporary-file resources it acquired for that cycle
